items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The band was now almost the same as the Original Lloyd Scott Bright Boys except for the drummer whose name was Arnold 'Scrip' Boling (L)... I joined Cecil.

ctx.x: After about six weeks with Russell, I began to feel the effects of not having a first part to play and only two solo spots, because we did not play 'Broadway Rhythm' where I had an eight-bar solo. Cecil Scott had reformed the Bright Boys under his name with a new drummer in place of Lloyd and had started working in the Savoy. I got lonesome for the 'Track' where I could socialize with the people and plus the fact that I was not satisfied with the role I was playing in Russell's band, so I went to see Cecil one…

The band was now almost the same as the Original Lloyd Scott Bright Boys except for the drummer whose name was Arnold 'Scrip' Boling (L) and a banjoist named Casper Tow ...... who was later replaced by James Smith. I felt the results of not having enough to play in Russell's band and it was almost two weeks before my chops began to get set and strong the way they had been before joining Russell. I was not disgusted with Red Allen because he blew more horn than I did. In fact I enjoyed hearing him play because he…

But I think that Russell could at least have let me play some first parts. I suppose he thought that I should be happy because I was playing in the Roseland, but that kind of prestige and under the conditions that I was playing, didn't mean a bag of beans to me and I love beans.
